extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and attorneys petitioning for reinstatement to practice before the USPTO; Office of Enrollment and Discipline stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Official decision on a petition for reinstatement to practice before the United States Patent and Trademark Office (Office of Enrollment and Discipline), describing the basis for granting reinstatement. Focuses on compliance with regulatory provisions and the Director's review of the petition and record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 37 CFR § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner must have 'complied with all provisions of 37 CFR § 11.58' on or before a specified date (here, on or before September 10, 2015).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This decision explicitly states that compliance with all provisions of 37 CFR § 11.58 is a predicate for reinstatement; the petition was granted because Mr. Hoekendijk 'complied with all provisions' by the stated date. The page does not reproduce § 11.58 text but identifies compliance with it as the controlling regulatory requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's review of petition and record material
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the Office of Enrollment and Discipline conducts a careful review of the Petition and all information in the record material to the petitioner's eligibility for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision notes that, after careful review of the petition and all record information material to eligibility, the Director determines whether reinstatement is 'appropriate.' This establishes that reinstatement is discretionary based on the petition plus supporting/record evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission and consideration of a Petition for Reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: A formal Petition for Reinstatement must be submitted and is placed into the record for consideration (the petition in this case was received on October 7, 2015).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The procedural fact of filing/receipt is recorded and is the triggering event for review. Though the page gives no filing-form detail, it demonstrates that timely submission and inclusion of material relevant to eligibility are part of the evaluation process.
